title: Necho II
summary: King of Egypt, son of Psammetichus (Herodotus "Necos", 2.158–159, 4.42); the Pharaoh-nechoh of 2 Kings 23 and Jeremiah 46.
description: Added from the Herodotus import (The Histories, tr. Rawlinson). Herodotus gives reign lengths and synchronisms, not BC years, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year (Herodotus is display-only and gives none).

reign.date: “After having reigned in all sixteen years, Necos died”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.159 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 166 (PDF p. 168)
reign.note: Necos defeated "the Syrians" at Magdolus and took Cadytis (2.159). DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): 525 + ½ + 44 + 25 + 6 = 600½, so Necos reigned about 617/616–601/600 BC (anchor CFAH AP-8). Consistent: Generations dates Carchemish (Pharaoh-necho, Jer 46:2) to 605 BC (provisional), inside the derived reign.

reign.date: “This discovery was first made by Necos, the Egyptian king, who on desisting from the canal which he had begun between the Nile and the Arabian gulf”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 4.42 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 259 (PDF p. 261)
reign.note: Necho's Phoenician ships sail round Libya (Africa).

reign.date: “it was not till the third year that they doubled the Pillars of Hercules, and made good their voyage home”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 4.42 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 260 (PDF p. 262)
reign.note: Length of the voyage: a little over two years.
